subject: OpsWorks private hosting: architecture review workshop (next steps)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@opsworks.com>, Priya Khanna <priya.khanna@opsworks.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: OpsWorks private hosting architecture review

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate you walking us through your main constraints (air-gapped staging, KMS requirements, and the stretched VPC between primary datacenter and DR site). Quick recap and proposal for next steps so we can get the technical review scheduled: 

Recap (from our discovery)
- Primary goal: validate a Private (VPC / on‑prem hybrid) design that meets OpsWorks data residency and audit requirements.
- Non-negotiables: customer-managed KMS, SOC2 audit logs, and regional isolation for production.
- Likely workstreams: network/connectivity, key management + secrets, model hosting (quantized variants), and ops/rollout plan.

Proposed next step
- 60-minute architecture workshop (technical deep dive) with your infra and SRE leads + our Private deployment engineers.
- Outcomes: high-level topology, required firewall/NAT rules, KMS/HSM integration approach, and a short mutual action plan (owners + timelines).

Availability (Pacific Time) — pick one: 
- Tue Apr 20 — 10:00–11:00 PT
- Wed Apr 21 — 09:00–10:00 PT or 14:00–15:00 PT

Attachments: opsworks-priv-arch-agenda.pdf (draft agenda) and opsworks-environment-matrix.xlsx (environment details we discussed). Please confirm who from your side will join (SRE, security, procurement) so we can invite the right folks.

If those slots don't work, tell me two windows that do and we will accommodate. Looking forward — we can also run the initial session as a quick 30-minute scoping call if you prefer.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Desai <samir.desai@opsworks.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Priya Khanna <priya.khanna@opsworks.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: OpsWorks private hosting architecture review

Connor —

Thanks for the clear recap. Priya (SRE) and I will be the primary attendees. Procurement may join for the mutual action plan section. A couple of notes before we lock a slot: 

- Air-gapped staging: we need to confirm that any install artifacts can be delivered via an approved scratch bundle; we likely cannot allow outbound connections from the staging cluster.
- KMS: our preference is Azure Key Vault in-managed HSM or a customer HSM appliance — happy to discuss both options.

Of the times you proposed, the following work for us (Pacific Time):
- Wed Apr 21 — 10:00–11:00 PT (this aligns with our SRE calendar)
- Thu Apr 22 — 14:00–15:00 PT (backup)

If you can put a calendar invitation on for Wed Apr 21 10:00 PT, that would be ideal. Please include a short pre-read and the agenda, and let us know if we should invite any additional internal teams.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Desai
Head of Infrastructure | OpsWorks Inc.
samir.desai@opsworks.com | +1 (617) 555-0198

What's included in the session:
- 10m — goals and success criteria (OpsWorks)
- 25m — proposed topology and network options (Redwood + OpsWorks constraints)

- 10m — open questions & next steps / mutual action plan

I'll invite our Private deployment engineer (Lauren Bishop) and Rishi from solutions engineering for the deep-dive. If there's anyone else on your side who should be present (network/security/procurement), reply-all with names and I'll add them.

See you Wednesday — I'll follow up with a calendar invite and a Teams link in ~15 minutes.

Samir / Priya / Connor —

Quick note ahead of Wed's workshop: we'll prepare a 2-slide primer on network requirements (NAT, firewall rules, and recommended ports for KV cache and model inference traffic). Also, do you want us to include a short section on LDAP/AD integration and SSO for admin access, or keep that for a follow-up deep dive?

If OpsWorks prefers LDAP on the call, we can add 10 minutes to the KMS section and bring a subject-matter expert.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
